candidate.title: Alchemy Tried in the Fire: Starkey, Boyle and the Fate of Helmontian Chymistry (review)

candidate.ask_addressed: What does the historiography (Newman and Principe on 'chymistry', Principe's work) say about whether alchemy and chemistry were separate? And what do sceptics say about popular claims that modern chemistry is simply 'Egyptian science', or that Hermes Trismegistus / the Emerald Tablet are pharaonic-era?
candidate.quote: Newman and Principe challenge the notion that the distinction between the two was so sharp
candidate.summary: A short journal review of Newman and Principe (Chicago, 2002). It reports their thesis that alchemy and chemistry were not sharply distinct, using Boyle and Starkey, and notes Boyle presented chemistry as separate from its alchemical roots.
candidate.limits: Review of a book, not the book; reviewer is not a specialist historian of chemistry as far as the page shows. Says nothing about Egypt.
